Cooper Norcross Health, formerly Cooper University Health Care, is a leading academic health system affiliated with Cooper Norcross Medical School of Rowan University. Headquartered in Camden, New Jersey, Cooper Norcross Health has revenues of more than $3 billion and an A+ credit rating from both S&P and Fitch Ratings.

Actuarial Studies

  • Analyses and research to improve pricing parameters and segmentation to better identify profitable opportunities

Tool Building

  • Designing, programming, maintaining, and supporting tools used in pricing, and book monitoring

title: Technical Specialist
description:
Job Summary:

Verifies and reports key operational data, forecasts, and contractual requirements to support the planning and balancing of generation levels, load demand, and system reserves. Monitors, evaluates, and tracks operational activities, projects, and procedures while collaborating across teams to ensure compliance, efficiency, and reliable electric system operations.

Job Description:

  • Verifies support tasks related to developing and managing Power Purchase Agreements (PPOAs), Joint Operating Procedures (JOPs), and other operational contracts with generating plants and market participants to ensure adequate power supply, operational reserves (spinning and standby), regulation reserves, Transmission Must Run (TMR), and zero‑power start‑up resources for normal and emergency operations.

  • Reports weekly generator availability forecasts, capacity projections, and hourly dispatch tables following established procedures to assist Transmission Center operators in maintaining system frequency and energy balance.

  • Monitors weekly load‑forecasting activities by gathering and analyzing operational data to help Transmission operators manage constraints, maintain energy balance, and prepare for potential emergencies.

  • Verifies that operational activities align with company policies, regulations, strategic plans, and agreements, including PPOAs, by applying documented procedures and compliance requirements.

  • Evaluates PPOA performance and collaborates with legal and regulatory teams to maintain documentation and support updates as needed.

  • Builds programs, processes, and procedures in collaboration with other System Operation teams and supports the implementation of systems and technologies that improve efficiency and service continuity.

  • Tracks new projects and proposed changes to existing operational standards, procedures, and reports, documenting findings and making recommendations to support reliable system operations.

  • Follows established company policies, procedures, and standards to ensure full compliance with applicable laws and industry regulations.

  • Participates in storm restoration tasks and assigned drills to contribute to the safe and reliable recovery of services.

  • Performs additional tasks aligned with role expectations and qualifications to support team goals and operational flexibility.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related field.

Experience

  • 0–3 years of hands-on experience in a technical or support role.
  • Preferred: Experience working with energy management systems, forecasting and dispatch tools, load‑analysis software, and platforms used to track contractual and operational requirements.

Competencies (Skills)

  • Operational Analysis: Applies analytical skills to interpret generation data, load forecasts, and system conditions to support reliable energy balancing.
  • Regulatory and Contract Compliance: Ensures operational activities follow established policies, procedures, and power purchase agreement requirements.
  • Cross‑Functional Collaboration: Works effectively with legal, regulatory, and system operation teams to maintain documentation, improve processes, and support operational continuity.
  • Process Development and Improvement: Builds and enhances operational programs, procedures, and systems to improve efficiency and service reliability.
  • Technical Reporting and Documentation: Prepares accurate operational reports, tracks project changes, and maintains records that support informed decision‑making and system planning.

  • Working in high places: Never

title: Adoptions & Behavior Counselor - Pima Animal Care Center
description:
Job Description Summary

Department - Pima Animal Care Center

Job Description

OPEN UNTIL FILLED


Job Type: Classified


Job Classification: 5931 - Animal Care Technician I


Salary Grade: 3


Hiring Pay: $18.79 Per Hour


The first review of applications will be on 10/02/2026.


Pima Animal Care Center (PACC) is looking to add a full-time Adoptions & Behavior Counselor to join our Outcomes Team. As an Adoptions & Behavior Counselor, you will work directly with our community to find the best furry friends for their home. This position is customer service centered and includes working both indoors and outdoors with dogs of varying behavior types. You will run large dog play groups, provide dog enrichment, and assess dog behavior.


PACC is open 7 days a week. Nontraditional work hours and rotating schedules.


Essential Functions:


As defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act, this classification may include any of the following tasks, knowledge, skills, and other characteristics. This list is ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY and is not a comprehensive listing of all functions and tasks performed by incumbents of this class. Work assignments may vary depending on the department’s need and will be communicated to the applicant or incumbent by the supervisor.


  • Provides humane care and safe handling for a variety of animals, including dogs, cats, and small pets, while monitoring behavior and health;
  • Works outdoors in all weather conditions and safely handles live animals, including those that may be injured, frightened, or offensive, using appropriate techniques to minimize risks to self and others;
  • Demonstrates excellent customer service to the public and volunteers by answering questions, addressing concerns, and guiding decisions regarding intakes, outcomes, redemptions and animal care in adherence to PACC policies;
  • Handles animals for behavioral assessments and playgroups, identifying placement or behavior concerns, and participates in decisions regarding outcomes, including euthanasia;
  • Accurately organizes and documents information on animal behavior, history, medical records and outcomes, utilizing shelter software and other systems for recordkeeping, communication, and scheduling;
  • Administers vaccinations and medications under veterinary guidance, assesses animals for signs of illness or injury and documents and communicates health concerns;
  • Facilitates adoption and foster processes by assisting with enrichment, behavioral evaluations, animal meet and greets, matchmaking and note reviews;
  • Supports intake and admissions by providing correct intake pathways, checking animals for health concerns, identifying ages/breeds and finding kennel placements;
  • Maintains a clean and sanitary facility, including kennels, workspaces, public lobbies, and treatment spaces;
  • Frequently lifts and carries heavy objects, bends, stoops, reaches, and performs other physical tasks as required;
  • Safeguards and accounts for scheduled drugs and funds received for PACC services;
  • Operates County-owned vehicles to transport animals and supplies.

Minimum Qualifications:


High school diploma or General Education Development (G.E.D.) certificate.


(Relevant experience and/or education from an accredited college or university may be substituted.)


Qualifying education and experience must be clearly documented in the "Education" and "Work Experience" sections of the application. Do not substitute a resume for your application or write "see resume" on your application.

Preferred Qualifications: (Be specific in describing your experience in your application. Ensure the descriptions provided illustrate your competencies, specifically addressing the required and preferred qualifications.):


  • Bilingual (English/Spanish).
  • Minimum one (1) year experience working in customer service.
  • Minimum one (1) year experience working or volunteering in an animal shelter or other relevant animal care setting.
  • Experience working or volunteering with dogs and/or cats.

Selection Procedure:
Pima County Human Resources Department reserves the right to admit to the selection process only those candidates that meet the minimum qualifications. All applications will be assessed based on an evaluation of the listed education and experience. Candidates meeting the minimum qualifications may be further evaluated/scored against any advertised Preferred Qualifications. The hiring authority will interview and select the successful candidate from a referral list provided by Human Resources. Additional assessments/testing may be required as part of the selection process.


Supplemental Information:


Licenses and Certificates: Some positions require a valid Arizona Class D driver license at the time of application or appointment. Failure to obtain/maintain the required licensure shall be grounds for termination.


Special Notice Items: The County requires pre-employment background checks. Successful candidates will receive a post-offer, pre-employment background screening to include verification of work history, education, and criminal conviction history. A prior criminal conviction will not automatically disqualify a candidate from employment with the County. Within nine months of appointment, employees must receive the full series of pre-exposure rabies immunizations. Medical inability to be immunized or previous immunization must be verified by the County Physician prior to employment. Recommended boosters are required for the duration of employment, unless medically excused or physiologically unable to develop immunity. This position will require a post-job offer physical and/or drug screen. This position will require post-job offer proof of immunization(s) or immunization(s) and/or a TB screening. Pima County determines whether a position is eligible for visa sponsorship at the time of recruitment. Eligibility is based on the requirements of the position and applicable laws and regulations. Not all positions with Pima County are eligible for visa sponsorship.


Physical/Sensory Requirements: Physical and sensory abilities will be determined by position. Action Activity - bending, climbing, crawling, kneeling, reaching, squatting, and stooping; Motion Activity - grasping; Hearing Activity - in noisy areas on a radio, behind themselves; Speaking Activity - in person, on a phone, on a radio; Vision - must be able to operate a motor vehicle, distinguish color, have depth perception, have peripheral vision. Frequently required to lift, push or pull objects weighing up to 100 pounds.


Working Conditions: Working conditions will be determined by position.

We are committed to an inclusive and diverse workforce and will not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, gender, sexual orientation, kinship, political interest, or any other characteristic protected by law.

description:

Supports and instructs those served by the department with complex queries, applies specialized knowledge of multiple standards, policies and procedures, and maintains accurate and detailed records.

Job Description:

The Arizona Center for Medieval and Renaissance Studies (ACMRS) is looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Program Manager to join our ongoing Mellon Foundation-funded RaceB4Race initiative. This is a full-time staff position, reporting to the ACMRS Portfolio Manager. The Program Manager will work on a variety of ACMRS projects; however, their main focus will be the “RB4R: Modeling a new Scholarly Community” award.

On the “RB4R: Modeling a new Scholarly Community” award, the Program Manager will:

  • Act as a central point of communication for all Throughlines scholars who, in collaboration with the ACMRS team, will create a full spectrum of premodern critical race studies content for use in higher education.

  • Be responsible for managing the external communication to these scholars including, but not limited to, content collection gathering, scheduling scholar filming, booking travel, reserving venues, and most importantly, making sure that clear expectations are communicated, and that all inquiries and follow-up messaging is completed in a responsive and timely manner.

  • Assist in communicating with multiple sub-award project teams, making sure they remain on-track with their various project activities.

Position Salary Range:

  • $60,000 - $70,000 DOE - this is a partially grant-funded position and is contingent on future grant funding.

Essential Duties:

  • Under direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager, the Program Manager will:

    • Work closely and collaboratively with ASU team members and invited scholars (see details above).

    • Help to manage and streamline external communication; track project scope, strategy, budget, and milestone outcomes; assist in monitoring project expectations; work on project administrative tasks.

    • Update project management software, purchase justifications, and draft reporting; and monitor project expectations with the team.

      • Specifically, the Program Manager will be responsible for monitoring, updating, and utilizing ACMRS’s project management software, Monday.com, to stay organized and on-track with all project activities. Most commonly, this software is how the ASU team tracks the progress of our Throughlines scholars’ content (written content, media content, supplementary materials, etc.).

    • Assist in preparing and maintaining all project status reports and schedules; track milestones/deliverables; and re-set expectations as needed in consideration of project progress/outcomes.

  • In collaboration with larger Center staff, the Program Manager will assist with running and organizing other concurrent events and programming including annual RB4R symposium and conference activities. Specifically they will:

    • Coordinate, arrange and manage the travel for speakers at ACMRS.

    • Assists in the management of the directors' calendars if/as needed.

    • Coordinate or assist in coordinating the center's events, including arranging equipment and catering, sending invitations and managing RSVPs.

    • Compile, prepare, and maintain background material related to meetings, events, and travel; coordinate and track follow-ups as needed.

    • Independently composes correspondence on a variety of subjects requiring judgement, originality, and knowledge of issues involved.

    • Provide back-up to other staff in the office.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Evidence of a bachelor’s degree or master’s degree

  • Has prior experience managing large-scale projects/activities.

  • Demonstrates knowledge of the principles and practices pertaining to the RaceB4Race initiative.

  • Skill in working with constituencies and clientele.

  • Experience in planning, analyzing and coordinating activities and establishing priorities.

  • Skill in establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills with a strong focus on collaboration and a high level of customer service.

  • Evidence of problem-solving, critical thinking and time management skills.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of relevant computer applications: Microsoft Office (i.e., Excel, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint), Dropbox, Google Drive, Slack, Workday, etc.

  • Experience working with Project Management systems such as Monday.com.

  • Ability and willingness to learn quickly and apply new skillsets.

  • Evidence of a diligent and reliable work ethic.

Working Environment:

  • Activities are primarily performed in a regular, climate-controlled office setting subject to extended periods of sitting

  • Use office equipment including a desktop computer. Lift up to 20 pounds

Department Statement:

The mission of ACMRS is to enable and promote the most expansive, creative, and daring scholarship in medieval and renaissance studies. We do this not only by fostering a vibrant intellectual community for the faculty at our three universities, but also by publishing forward-looking, vanguard research through our in-house press. ACMRS promotes work that is historically grounded and theoretically expansive, with the aim of advancing dialogues that reach into the present moment and point us to different, more inclusive, futures.

Driving Requirement:

Driving is not required for this position.

Campus: Tempe

No Federal Funding

title: Plant Operator - Intermediate
description:
#WeAreONEOK – Fortune 500 company. 100+ years in business. Leading midstream service provider. Safety first. Sustainable operations. Environmentally responsible. Employee focused.

JOB SUMMARY

The Plant Operator is responsible for the safe and efficient operation, monitoring, and maintenance of natural gas and liquids processing facilities while supporting reliable plant performance and production goals. This role operates and maintains critical equipment including compressors, motors, engines, pumps, turbines, cooling systems, treating units, and other process equipment, while monitoring operating conditions and responding to changing plant needs. Responsibilities include starting and stopping equipment, preparing systems for maintenance through permitting and lockout/tagout procedures, assisting with mechanical repairs and troubleshooting, maintaining operational and safety records, and supporting environmental and regulatory compliance efforts. The ideal candidate has a strong mechanical aptitude, an understanding of gas and liquids processing operations, and a commitment to safety, teamwork, and operational excellence in a hands-on industrial environment.Job Profile Summary

Performs activities related to operation and maintenance of oil and gas liquid processing facilities under supervision.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

  • Operate and maintain processing plant equipment including, but not limited to:
    • Compressors
    • Motors
    • Engines
    • Cooling equipment
    • Auxiliary units
    • Pumps
    • Turbines
    • Treating systems

  • Monitor and control equipment operating conditions
  • Start, stop, and operate equipment
  • Prepare equipment for maintenance activities including, but not limited to:
    • Permitting
    • Lock out tag out
    • Decommissioning

  • Assist mechanics and others in performing repairs to equipment
  • Identify and report any safety and/or environmental concerns
  • Compile and/or maintain information such as time sheets, work logs, safety/environmental forms, and equipment maintenance and repair records
  • Drive and ensure maintenance is complete on company vehicles
  • Responsibilities may include Department of Transportation (DOT) covered functions, including operations, maintenance, or emergency response on a pipeline. Job duties also require the employee to be alert and respond immediately to dangerous or hazardous conditions, and where impaired performance, or failure to follow safety precautions, could result in serious injury or property damage.

Education

  • None Required.

Work Experience

  • Experience reading and interpreting drawings, diagrams, work logs, dials, gauges, charts, procedures, and operational and repair manuals

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of: compressor station, storage field, gathering field, and/or processing plant operations
  • Knowledge of: computers. Demonstrated ability to access and/or perform basic computer functions utilizing company software applications
  • Knowledge of: gas and liquid processing fundamentals
  • Knowledge of: applicable company and governmental operating practices and procedures
  • Knowledge of: safe handling of flammable gases, liquids, and high-pressure systems
  • Ability to: analyze, adjust, and perform minor repairs on equipment
  • Ability to: apply addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division
  • Ability to: maintain and prepare information such as safety/environmental reports, work logs, maintenance/repair logs, and time sheets
  • Ability to: interact and communicate effectively
  • Ability to: communicate and/or exchange information and instructions

Licenses and Certifications

  • Applicable certifications required

Strength Factor Rating - Physical Demands/Requirements

  • Heavy Work - Exerting 50 to 100 pounds of force occasionally and/or 25 to 50 pounds of force frequently and/or 10 to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Physical Demand requirements are in excess of those for Medium Work.

title: Programme Manager
description:
Job Description

Programme Manager – Manufacturing Operations

Derby - Hybrid
Full time


The Programme Manager – Manufacturing Operations is responsible for the planning, monitoring and control of all aspects of the programme, and the motivation of those involved, to achieve the business objectives and outcomes within the expected programme performance targets of schedule, cost, quality, scope, benefits and risks.


You will own and lead a programme of site-based Manufacturing Operations projects, in accordance with S9, the Facilities Project Model and Project Management Office governance as required. The programme will involve executing relevant elements of the Manufacturing Operations portfolio, working closely with Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Services and Planning & Control, as well as potentially several external contractors.


The role supports hybrid working, with a normal balance of three days per week in the office. The programme currently includes projects across Ansty, Annesley and Derby, and you will be expected to travel to other plants within the Compression Systems MBU as required to support project deliver


What you will be doing:

  • Accountable for the successful delivery to cost, specification and time of defined packages of work within the programme.
  • Secure and manage the provision of resources required for the programme from internal and/or external providers.
  • Create and manage an integrated set of programme plans and schedules.
  • Develop and secure budgets for the programme and control forecast and actual costs against the allocated budget.
  • Establish, develop and maintain the documentation necessary to deliver the package(s) of work within the programme.
  • Act as the focal point and escalation route for all aspects relating to the packages of work within the programme.
  • Lead and coordinate multi-functional teams to support successful programme delivery.
  • Adapt plans and priorities within your area to address resource and operational challenges and maintain delivery against programme objectives.

Position Qualifications:

  • At least 5 years’ experience in project or programme management, or equivalent relevant industry experience.
  • Demonstrable experience of planning, monitoring and controlling projects or programmes against schedule, cost, quality, scope, benefits and risk.
  • Experience of managing integrated plans and schedules, budgets, resources and delivery performance.
  • Experience of leading and coordinating teams and stakeholders to deliver defined outcomes.
  • Strong knowledge of project/programme management principles, governance and delivery disciplines.
  • Ability to operate autonomously within defined standards and policies, escalating where the impact is broader or the subject matter is more complex.
  • Strong decision-making and problem-solving capability, with the ability to adapt plans and priorities in response to resource and operational challenges.
  • Degree-level qualification or equivalent relevant industry experience.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Experience of leading multi-functional teams.
  • Experience of delivering projects or programmes within Manufacturing Operations or a related manufacturing environment.
  • Experience of working with Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Services and Planning & Control functions.
  • Experience of managing internal and external providers or contractors.
  • Membership of a relevant professional body, or working towards an appropriate professional qualification.
  • Knowledge or experience of S9, Facilities Project Model and/or PMO governance.

Our vision is to ensure that the excellence and ingenuity that shaped our history continues into our future. Our multi-year transformation programme aims to turn Rolls-Royce into a high-performing, competitive, resilient and growing company. Join us, and it can be your future vision too.


Rolls-Royce are committed to being a respectful, inclusive, and non-discriminatory workplace where individuality is valued, diverse perspectives fuel innovation, and everyone can thrive.

title: Senior Director - People Relations and Compliance
location: Spring, Texas, United States of America
description:
Senior Director - People Relations and Compliance

Description -

The People Relations & Compliance (PRC) Lead is responsible for leading global Employee Relations (ER), Labor Relations (LR), and HR Compliance functions. This role owns the strategic direction, governance, and delivery model across all three pillars, ensuring consistent, compliant, and business-aligned practices globally, as a unified, high-impact People Relations & Compliance Center of Excellence (CoE).

The PRC Lead acts as a trusted advisor to senior executive leadership on complex people matters, driving resolution of high-risk and high-visibility cases while strengthening compliance frameworks and proactive risk mitigation. This role partners closely with People Leadership teams, Centers of Excellence (CoEs), Legal, and business leaders to deliver a scalable, efficient, and future-ready operating model.

As People Relations & Compliance Lead, you will:

  • Lead Employee Relations, Labor Relations, and HR Compliance pillars under a single People Relations & Compliance CoE model

  • Lead PRC transformation and operating model, governance, and RACI across global, regional, and business-aligned teams

  • Drive standardization of policies, processes, and tools, ensuring global consistency with local flexibility

  • Lead resolution of complex, high-risk, and senior executive escalation cases, partnering closely with Legal and senior stakeholders

  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior executives and People leaders on people risk, compliance, and organizational decisions

  • Enable clear ownership between PRC, HRBPs, and stakeholders, reducing duplication and improving delivery effectiveness

  • Partner across Centers of Excellence (CoEs) to ensure integrated, seamless delivery of people-related initiatives

  • Build, develop, and coach a high-performing PRC team, strengthening capabilities and future readiness

  • Leverage AI, automation, and data-driven insights to elevate the function, improve efficiency, and enhance decision-making

  • Drive a proactive, forward-looking approach to people risk and compliance, anticipating issues and enabling early intervention

  • Lead the transformation towards a strategic, customer-focused, and high-impact PRC function, simplifying processes and improving outcomes

To be selected for this role, you will also need to be/have:

  • Global organizational leadership experience / Extensive ER/LR/Compliance leadership experience in a global, matrixed environment

  • Proven track record managing senior executive escalations and high-risk employee relations cases

  • Strong compliance and legal acumen, with ability to interpret and operationalize complex regulatory requirements

  • Deep expertise in labor relations, including collective bargaining and workforce negotiations

  • Experience leading or operating within a Center of Excellence (CoE) model, including cross-functional coordination

  • Ability to operate strategically and operationally, balancing governance with execution

  • Proven ability to lead organizational transformation and drive change at scale

  • High degree of discretion and strict adherence to confidentiality.

  • Strong project and process management skills. Excellent planning, time management, prioritization, and organizational skills as well as the ability to handle competing priorities calmly under pressure and within restricted timeframes

  • Solid communication (written and verbal), interpersonal, and the ability to deal effectively and professionally with all levels of employees and management

  • Excellent relationship building and management, as well as leadership and influencing skills (particularly at Executive Level)

Education and Experience

  • A minimum of 15 years of progressive HR experience across different HR functions, specifically including Employee Relations, Labor Relations & HR Compliance

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Labor Relations, Law, Business Administration, or any other related discipline or commensurate work experience or demonstrated competence.

This job description describes the general nature and level of work performed in this role. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, skills, responsibilities, knowledge, etc. These may be subject to change and additional functions may be assigned as needed by management.

The pay range for this role is 200,000 - 300,000.00 annually with additional opportunities for pay in the form of bonus and/or equity (applies to United States of America candidates only). Pay varies by work location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Benefits:

  • Flexible spending account

title: Plumbing Drain Technician - Marietta
description:
Overview

Residential Drain Technician

Mr. Plumber is looking for a dependable, customer-focused Plumber to join our growing team. In this role, you’ll help homeowners diagnose and resolve residential plumbing issues while providing professional, high-quality service.

If you enjoy hands-on work, solving problems, working independently, and making a real difference for homeowners, we’d love to hear from you!

What You’ll Do

  • Diagnose, repair, and install residential plumbing systems and components.

  • Troubleshoot plumbing issues involving water lines, drains, toilets, faucets, water heaters, and other residential plumbing systems.

  • Perform plumbing repairs and installations according to company standards and applicable codes.

  • Identify the root cause of plumbing problems and clearly communicate findings to homeowners.

  • Explain recommended repairs and solutions in a way homeowners can easily understand.

  • Provide customers with options for resolving identified plumbing issues and obtain approval before completing additional work.

  • Perform drain cleaning and other plumbing services when needed.

  • Use plumbing tools, diagnostic equipment, sewer cameras, and other equipment as required.

  • Remove and replace plumbing fixtures and components as necessary to complete repairs.

  • Maintain accurate service documentation using company technology.

  • Keep your company vehicle, tools, and equipment clean, organized, stocked, and properly maintained.

  • Follow all company safety policies, procedures, and quality standards.

  • Respect customers’ homes and property by maintaining a clean and professional work environment.

  • Communicate effectively with dispatch, management, and other members of the team.

What We’re Looking For

  • Previous residential plumbing experience preferred.

  • Strong knowledge of residential plumbing systems and repair practices.

  • Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to diagnose plumbing issues and determine appropriate solutions.

  • Comfortable working in crawl spaces, tight areas, and varying indoor and outdoor conditions.

  • Excellent communication and customer service skills.

  • Ability to explain technical issues in a way homeowners can easily understand.

  • Self-motivated and able to work independently.

  • Professional appearance and positive attitude.

  • Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.

  • Ability to pass required background and pre-employment screening.

Why Join Mr. Plumber?

At Mr. Plumber, we believe our people are the foundation of our success. We provide the training, tools, and support you need to build a long-term career in the home services industry.

We Offer

  • Competitive compensation

  • Performance-based bonus opportunities

  • Company-provided vehicle and equipment

  • Paid technical training and ongoing development

  • Tool purchasing assistance

  • Boot allowance

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Paid time off and paid holidays

  • Family-friendly scheduling

  • Career advancement opportunities

  • A team-oriented work environment

Grow Your Career With Us

This position is a great opportunity for an experienced Residential Plumber who wants to grow within the plumbing industry. For the right individual, there are opportunities to expand your technical knowledge, develop additional skills, and advance within the organization.

If you take pride in your work, enjoy helping people, and want to build a career—not just find another job—we want to meet you!

Mr. Plumber is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

What Will I Do?

  • Camera and diagnose sewer and mainline plumbing problems and provide cost estimates to the customer
  • Provide solutions to sewer, drain and mainline problems

Qualifications

  • Knowledge of residential and commercial plumbing
  • Mechanical aptitude
  • Professional appearance and grooming

title: Multimedia Systems Engineer III
description:
Overview

Abacus Technology is seeking a Multimedia Systems Engineer to provide technical support and oversight of the design, development, implementation, and life cycle management of complex multimedia, A/V, imagery, and broadcast systems for the eMITS program at Johnson Space Center. This is a full-time position.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, build, and integration of complex multimedia, broadcast, A/V, and imagery systems.
  • Provide technical analysis for new hardware systems, upgrades, risk assessments, and implementation plans.
  • Draft detailed engineering plans, analyses, workflows, and cost estimations.
  • Provide project oversight for installation, maintenance, and operations staff.
  • Assign, track, and ensure compliance of personnel work activities.
  • Manage financial planning, forecasting, reconciliation, and budget tracking of engineering projects.
  • Oversee creation, tracking, and reconciliation of complex PRs, POs, vendor invoices, and purchasing assignments.
  • Provide senior expertise on Dalet and its integrations across NASA (IO and eMITS).
  • Support legacy conference rooms, CATV modernization approaches, IPTV integration in B8, WAN video deployment, satellite reception systems, and public distribution at JSC.
  • Manage bitstream recorders in B8 and B30 and plan for format migration of NASA video repositories.
  • Support parsing and transition of VRPS system components to other organizational users.
  • Contribute to plans and issue resolution for Teague Auditorium and other key NASA facilities.
  • Support eMITS relationship with AEGIS including dark fiber configurations and network considerations.

Qualifications

9+ years experience in engineering for television and A/V systems. Bachelor’s degree in Electronics or a related field. Additional years of experience may be substituted for degree requirements. Member or Certified by the ADDA or ADDA (digital) program preferred. PMP or equivalent project management certification or experience preferred. Certification or training in systems architecture or enterprise IT modernization preferred. Must have strong project management, financial management, and system integration experience. Strong knowledge of multimedia and broadcast systems, system design principles, AutoCAD, and electronics engineering. Experience administering Vault and MPulse systems, including drafting standards, release modes, and engineering documentation workflows. Familiarity with NASA or federal procurement systems (e.g., SAP, Deltek, Oracle) for managing PRs, POs, and vendor invoicing. Extensive knowledge of SMPTE standards, NEC codes, A/V requirements, and industry best practices. Experience managing technical crews and coordinating work with General Contractors. Expertise in the latest version of AutoCAD drafting software. Knowledge of databases and A/V drafting schemas. Experience with analog and digital baseband over copper; CATV over copper; analog and digital baseband over short haul fiber optics; facility automation systems; physical and virtual isochronous routing systems; Internet Protocol Television (IPTV); camera control; audio mixing systems; digital switching systems; and multimedia control systems. Experience coordinating with NASA facility teams, including dig permits, Mission Control Center interfaces (B8/B30), and SCH protocols preferred. Hands-on experience with Dalet, Evertz, Cobalt, Ross, Sony and Sencore systems. An understanding of satellite reception systems and IP-based video content distribution networks used in NASA or similar enterprise environments desired. Demonstrated leadership in guiding system architecture transitions and modernization efforts preferred. Able to analyze complex systems, identify gaps, and independently develop solutions. Experience supporting NASA, aerospace, DoD, or other large federal technical environments desired. Proficient in AutoCAD and Microsoft 365 as well as SharePoint and Box. Experience working in sensitive or mission-critical environments, with awareness of federal IT security protocols and data handling standards. Able to think, plan, and work independently while meeting deadlines. Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to interact effectively with employees, customers, and cross-functional teams. Excellent organizational skills and commitment to staying current with emerging technologies. Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and provide daily/weekly project reporting. Must be a US citizen.

The projected compensation range for this position is $85,200-$106,800. There are multiple factors that can impact a final salary, including, but not limited to, Contract Wage Determination, relevant work experience, skills and competencies that align to the specified role, geographic location (if remote or different from the stated location for this position), education and certifications as well as Federal Government Contract Labor categories. In addition, Abacus Technology offers a benefits package that includes: Health and Dental Insurance; 401(k) and Matching; Life Insurance; Short- and Long-Term Disability; Paid Time Off; Paid Holidays; and Professional Membership, Technical Training, Certification, and Education Assistance.

Applicants selected will be subject to a U.S. government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.

title: Lease Operator
description:
Job Description:

Permian Resources (NYSE: PR) is currently seeking a Lease Operator in San Angelo, TX. This position is responsible for overseeing the daily oil and gas well testing, operating and maintenance of assigned oil and gas process equipment. This including the identification of problems, documentation, and production reporting. The ideal candidate will have strong technical as well as communication skills and be able to contribute his/her expertise while working on multi-disciplinary team in a fast-paced environment.

General Responsibilities

  • Gauge production and perform operational checks on assigned wells, equipment and facilities.

  • Perform lease maintenance, such as minor production repairs and maintaining a clean working environment.

  • Maintain heater, separator, and other pressure vessels to company standards.

  • Maintain fluid pumps.

title: Senior HRIS Analyst
description:
Whether you’re a recent grad or a seasoned professional, you can experience meaningful career growth at Rosendin. Enjoy a true sense of ownership as you work with a proven industry leader on some of the most exciting and high-profile projects in the nation. We offer a wide range of job opportunities, competitive compensation, full benefits, an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and more.

Why Rosendin?

Committed. Innovative. Engaged.

If you’re looking to take your career to the next level and work with some of the best and brightest in the industry, we want to hear from you. Since our founding over 100+ years ago, Rosendin has been driven to positively impact the communities where we live and work. We are an organization built on integrity, and we have a culture that empowers people, embraces diversity, and inspires everyone to do their best. As one of the largest EMPLOYEE-OWNED electrical contractors in the United States, you will have the unique benefit of being a shareholder at a company that is experiencing tremendous growth and success. When our people succeed and fuel our success, we reward them. We’d love to have you as a shareholder!



YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY:

The Senior HRIS Analyst owns Workday data integrity, reporting, and release validation as an end-to-end area of responsibility — determining how issues get resolved and how the work gets done, rather than executing under close direction. This role sets the day-to-day standard for data accuracy and system reliability across Rosendin's HR technology systems, with Workday as the primary platform, and is trusted to design and implement solutions to data and configuration problems independently rather than escalate them or rely on consultants by default. The Senior HRIS Analyst partners directly with managers across HR Operations and adjacent functions, representing the HRIS function in cross-functional working sessions rather than responding to requests from the sidelines. This role reports to the HRIS Manager, is one of two Senior HRIS Analysts on the team, and partners regularly with the Process Optimization Program Manager, HR Technology, Payroll, Compensation, Benefits, Learning & Development, Talent Acquisition, and IT.


WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Data Integrity & System Administration

  • Own data integrity for Workday end-to-end, independently diagnosing and resolving complex data and configuration issues as well as recommending mitigation solutions rather than escalating routine problems.
  • Process mass data changes and business process configuration, setting the approach for how recurring issues get fixed as well recommending solutions for complex issues rather than following a predefined playbook.
  • Own user access and security role administration, including periodic regular audits, and recommend adjustments to standards and process as the platform evolves.
  • Provide data and administrative support across other HR technology systems as needed (e.g., ATS, LMS), determining the right approach in partnership with the HRIS Manager rather than working solely under direction.

Reporting & Analytics

  • Independently design, build, and maintain the core Workday reporting suite, partnering directly with HR and business managers to define requirements rather than simply fulfilling requests.
  • Own recurring workforce reporting and compliance-related data submissions, incorporating compliance considerations into report design from the outset, as well as proactively updating and evolving reporting and data compliance requirements.
  • Apply calculated fields, advanced report-writing tools, and Excel-based analysis to solve complex reporting problems that don't have an established template.

Testing & Release Management

  • Own the execution and validation of Workday release testing end-to-end, determining test strategy and coordinating across stakeholders rather than executing scripts under direction.
  • Create comprehensive UAT Project Plan that outlines and includes: scope & success criteria; test plan & test scripts, stakeholders & testers, timeline with milestones for all test groups, and cutover plan w/ hypercare scope/time.
  • Document test results and defects, and independently triage and resolve complex configuration issues identified during testing cycles, escalating only what genuinely requires the HRIS Manager's involvement.

User Support, Documentation & Process Improvement

  • Serve as the senior front-line resource for Workday questions and issues, resolving the majority of requests independently through direct WD configurations and escalating only genuinely novel problems.
  • Own the documentation library — job aids, process documentation, and standard operating procedures — for consistent system use across HR Operations.
  • Identify and configure independently complex process and system improvement opportunities from day-to-day system use and data trends, and bring fully-formed recommendations to the HRIS Manager rather than raw observations.
  • Represent the HRIS function in cross-functional working sessions with managers across HR Operations and adjacent functions on system and data questions.
  • Coordinate day-to-day with the other Senior HRIS Analyst to divide ownership across functional areas and cover for one another during peak periods or absences.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL:

  • Strong working knowledge of Workday data structures, security architecture, and business process configuration.
  • Demonstrated experience independently creating and implementing complex Workday configuration solutions to day-to-day system process and usage, data and reporting, and security administration.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve data and configuration problems independently, without a predefined solution to follow.
  • Strong information and data analytical skills, comfortable building reporting solutions to problems that don't have an established template.
  • Well-developed communication skills, able to represent HRIS work credibly in front of managers and cross-functional partners.
  • Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills, capable of managing multiple technical priorities simultaneously.
  • Proficient in Workday and Microsoft Office Suite, including advanced Excel.

WHAT YOU BRING TO US:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 5-7 years of experience in HRIS or HR technology, with demonstrated ownership of data integrity, reporting, or release testing work.
  • Strong demonstrated hands-on experience and knowledge in Workday HCM
  • Proficient hands-on experience and knowledge of at least 1 Workday Modules (Performance, Advanced Compensation, Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, etc.)
  • Working knowledge and understanding of Workday Education and Workday Learning Center for at least 1 Workday Modules (Performance, Advanced Compensation, Talent Acquisition, etc.)
  • Demonstrated experience using Workday Community to research options/solutions/answers and providing recommendations to HRIS Manager based on WD business requests.
  • A track record of solving data and configuration problems independently rather than working solely from defined instructions.
  • Experience partnering directly with managers or cross-functional stakeholders on system and data matters.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • General work environment – sitting for long periods, standing, walking, typing, carrying, pushing, bending. Work is conducted primarily indoors with varying environmental conditions such as fluorescent lighting and air conditioning
  • Noise level is usually low to medium; it can be loud on the jobsite.
  • We fully comply with the ADA and applicable state law, including considering reasonable accommodation measures that may enable qualified disabled applicants and employees to perform essential functions.
  • Occasional lifting of up to 30 lbs

YOU Matter – Our Benefits

  • ESOP – Employee Stock Ownership
  • 401 K
  • Annual bonus program based upon performance, profitability, and achievement
  • 17 PTO days per year plus 10 paid holidays
  • 3 days of paid sick leave each year
  • 3 days of paid Bereavement leave each year

  • Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance

  • Term Life, AD&D Insurance, and Voluntary Life Insurance
  • Disability Income Protection Insurance
  • Pre-tax Flexible Spending Plans (Health and Dependent Care)
  • Charitable Giving Match with our Rosendin Foundation

Our success is rooted in our people. We all come together around long-term vision and a sense of shared ownership. As a group, we do whatever it takes to ensure the success of our business…and your career.

title: Software Engineer in Test, Humanoid Robotics
description:
Boston Dynamics seeks a highly technical Software Engineer in Test, to test the Atlas Humanoid Robot. In this critical, hands-on role, you will be responsible for ensuring the reliability, safety, and performance of Atlas’s software systems, focusing heavily on metrics based system testing for reliability and performance.


A key quality to be successful in this role is the exceptional ability to context-switch and rapidly acquire technical understanding across diverse domains: from web interfaces and network protocols to robot behavior and ML model validation. If you thrive on learning fast, solving cross-functional problems, and seeing your code directly impact a groundbreaking robot, this role is for you.


Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. Now we are quickly becoming a recognized leader in automation solutions for industrial applications and warehouse logistics.


What You’ll Do:


  • Test & Automation Design: Design, develop, and maintain the comprehensive manual and automated overall regression test suite, focusing on integration stability. You will focus heavily on validating our teleoperation systems and action sequencing applications.
  • Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Testing: Perform automated testing with physical hardware in the loop, executing actual sequencing setups, physical interventions, and real-time robotic test runs.
  • XR Applications Testing: Drive the end-to-end quality of virtual environments by designing both automated and manual testing strategies for VR and Unity-based applications used in robot simulation and operator teleoperation.
  • Release Contribution & Reporting: Contribute to generating detailed Test Execution Reports for major milestones and releases, clearly documenting coverage and communicating quality status to the manager and development teams.
  • Process Improvement: Identify bottlenecks and gaps in the SQA process and testing coverage, driving continuous improvement in execution efficiency and reliability.

Required Experience:


  • 3–4 years of experience in Software QA Engineering, Test Automation, or Software Development, with a history of shipping and supporting product releases.
  • Hands-on experience with Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) manual testing, including physical test setup manipulation and live sequencing execution on robotics, automotive, or embedded systems.
  • Strong proficiency in test automation with a solid base in Python, C#, or a similar language. Direct experience automating HTTP and WebSocket (WS) APIs is required.
  • Demonstrated experience testing LLM / VLM systems, including evaluating model responses via manual prompting, API layers, and setting up quality assessment metrics.
  • Experience executing both automated and manual test strategies for VR and Unity-based applications, simulation software, or interactive 3D environments.
  • Expertise in designing comprehensive test plans and executing functional, integration, and regression testing with strong manual rigor.
  • Expertise in Defect Lifecycle Management using defect tracking systems (e.g., Jira) for precise defect reporting, verification, and analysis.
  • Solid understanding of CI/CD practices and experience integrating and monitoring automated tests within continuous integration tools (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI).

Nice to Have Experience:


  • Experience testing real-time control systems or low-latency teleoperation hardware/software.
  • Familiarity with UI/UX and backend validation for complex workflow sequencing or orchestration applications.
  • Operational familiarity with a Linux development environment (e.g., advanced bash/shell scripting).
  • Experience with Root Cause Analysis on complex, cross-functional system failures.

We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.


The salary range for this position will be clearly stated in the job posting as required by Massachusetts law. The base pay range for this position is between $88,,000 - $110,000. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting.

description:
Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.


Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.


Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.


As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.


We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.


We're looking for a Vault Processing Lead to join our PSA Vault Operations team to guide daily processing operations and serve as a subject matter expert while ensuring the highest standards of accuracy and service excellence for our collectors. This hands-on leadership role requires someone who can run shifts in the absence of supervisors, lead by example, and mentor team members while maintaining meticulous attention to detail. You'll be instrumental in upholding our commitment that every item—regardless of value—receives exceptional care and accuracy throughout the processing workflow.

You'll report to the Vault Operations Supervisor and work from our New Castle, DE facility.

The schedule will be Sunday- Wednesday or Wed to Saturday 7:00am- 5:30pm

What You'll Do:

  • Catalog incoming inventory with meticulous attention to detail, accurately identifying graded versus ungraded items while adhering to established style and content rules—because we simply have to get it right

  • Run shifts when supervisors are not present, serving as the primary point of contact and ensuring smooth operations while leading with integrity

  • Monitor and report on key shift metrics including throughput completed, items shipped, and work remaining for the next shift to process

  • Conduct thorough research on items and communicate proactively with Client Partners regarding additional services and condition assessments, always starting with why and providing context

  • Mentor and guide team members by sharing your expertise and knowledge, fostering an environment of continuous learning and bringing out the best in everyone

  • Perform and oversee inventory audits, quality control checks, and accuracy verification to ensure items are in correct locations both physically and systematically

  • Put inventory into storage locations and systemically locate inventory with precision

  • Organize picking tickets efficiently to provide for on-time shipping, balancing efficiency with care—treating every item as special

  • Pick inventory from designated locations and stage for packing and shipping

  • Pack and ship inventory following prescribed packing methods and generate shipping labels

  • Systemically and physically move items into designated storage or staging locations

  • Operate material handling equipment safely to move products within the warehouse

  • Put the skunk on the table—sharing challenges or concerns transparently so problems can be addressed quickly

  • Seek feedback early and often to continuously improve processes and quality

  • Safely handle and account for valuable merchandise, ensuring its security and proper handling throughout all process stages


Who You Are:

  • Someone who leads with integrity—making honest, ethical decisions and understanding that trust is our brand

  • Obsessed with serving the collector first, working backwards from their needs and treating every item with the care it deserves

  • Committed to getting it right consistently—possessing exceptional attention to detail, research skills, and a sharp eye for defects or misalignments

  • Kind and respectful in all interactions—assuming positive intent, displaying empathy, and being constructive when providing guidance

  • Able to communicate effectively both in writing and verbally, providing context and ensuring others understand the goal and why

  • Highly organized with strong problem-solving abilities, thriving in high-paced environments while maintaining focus and quality standards

  • Someone who thinks "yes" before "no"—exploring how something might work and embracing solutions that benefit collectors long-term

  • Self-aware and always willing to learn and grow, embracing feedback as a gift and sharing knowledge generously with team members

  • Able to work collaboratively in close team environments while mentoring others and leading by example

  • Detail-oriented with the ability to focus on individual tasks over extended periods without sacrificing accuracy

  • Reliable and prepared—showing up on time with a positive attitude and ready to lead when called upon

  • Comfortable running shifts independently and making operational decisions in the absence of supervisors

  • High school diploma or equivalent education background preferred, or equivalent work experience

  • Associate's degree in relevant field preferred


Physical Requirements

  • Bending and Twisting: Bending neck/waist, twisting neck/waist, and squatting.

  • Computer Use: Typing, mouse work, and sitting and looking at a computer potentially for long periods of time.

  • Hand Use: Regular hand use for various tasks.

  • Hearing Requirements: Ability to hear alarms, signals, and verbal instructions.

  • Receiving and Inspecting Submissions: Ability to receive, and in some departments inspect, submissions. Ability to use a sharp blade and retrieve submissions from packaging.

  • Sitting or Standing: Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time.

title: Family Services Specialist
description:

DISTINGUISHING FEATURES OF THE CLASS: Provides service coordination and case management to families of children with special needs. These duties involve the responsibility for rendering case management, assess­ment, referral and planning services to children and families. Individual is responsible for identifying and coordinating needed services as shown by individual family service plan on each individual client. Work is performed under the supervision of the Director of Public Health. Performs related duties as required.

Shape the Future of Workforce Change at FNZ



FNZ is seeking an Employee Relations Lead to join our People & Culture team on a 12-month fixed-term contract.


This is a unique opportunity to play a pivotal role in supporting organisational change and workforce transformation initiatives across FNZ. Working at the centre of complex change programmes, you will provide expert employee relations guidance, and ensure change is delivered in a way that is commercially effective, legally and regulatory compliant, and aligned to FNZ's values.


You'll partner closely with senior business leaders and our teams to design and deliver workforce consultation strategies that support organisational objectives while maintaining employee engagement and minimising risk.



The Opportunity


This is the perfect opportunity for a People Business partner that specialises in Employee Relations.


You'll lead workforce programmes across a global organisation, helping leaders navigate organisational change while ensuring compliance with employment legislation and best practice employee relations principles.


The role offers the opportunity to influence senior stakeholders, shape workforce change strategies and deliver high-profile organisational initiatives that have a meaningful impact across FNZ.


What You'll Be Doing


Workforce Execution Leadership

  • Lead complex workforce change activities across multiple business areas
  • Design and implement change strategies aligned to business objectives and legal requirements
  • Support business leaders through organisational design and workforce change initiatives
  • Develop clear communication plans and engagement strategies throughout change programmes

Organisational Change

  • Partner with senior stakeholders to plan and execute organisational change initiatives
  • Support workforce optimisation programmes
  • Advise on employment risks associated with organisational change activities
  • Ensure robust governance, documentation and decision-making frameworks are maintained
  • Manage complex employee relations issues arising from change programmes
  • Support the delivery of sustainable organisational outcomes whilst balancing employee and commercial considerations

Employee Relations Expertise

  • Act as a trusted adviser on complex employee relations matters
  • Provide practical guidance on UK employment law and consultation requirements
  • Partner with Legal and HR teams to ensure consistent risk management approaches
  • Support senior leaders in managing sensitive and high-profile employee situations
  • Identify and mitigate employee relations, legal and reputational risks
  • Promote best practice employee relations across the organisation

Stakeholder Management & Influence

  • Build trusted relationships with senior business leaders and People teams
  • Influence decision-making through expert advice and evidence-based recommendations
  • Facilitate discussions with key stakeholders during periods of organisational change
  • Provide regular updates to governance forums and leadership teams
  • Ensure alignment across business, HR and Legal stakeholders throughout change programmes

Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Ensure workforce change activities comply with UK employment legislation and regulatory requirements
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation and audit trails
  • Identify risks, issues and dependencies across change programmes
  • Support governance reporting and escalation processes where required
  • Drive consistent and compliant approaches across all workforce change initiatives



What We're Looking For


  • Significant Employee Relations experience within a complex organisation
  • Proven experience leading large-scale workforce transformation, or organisational change programmes
  • Extensive knowledge of UK employment law
  • Experience managing complex stakeholder groups and influencing senior leaders
  • Demonstrable experience operating within professional services, financial services, consulting or private equity-backed organisations
  • Strong commercial awareness with the ability to balance business and employee considerations
  • Experience working in fast-paced and evolving business environments
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and influencing skills
  • Strong project and programme delivery capabilities

  • Six (6) years progressively responsible experience in finance, risk management, or another related field, including areas such as liability claims management, workers compensation, DOT/FTA-mandated substance abuse testing programs, and Texas commercial motor vehicle driver regulations.
  • Experience leading people, including managing and directing a professional staff.
  • Experience leading change, including developing and implementing new policies and procedures.
  • Experience building coalitions with supervisors, peers, and subordinates; experience working with a board of directors preferred but not required.

  • Knowledge of Federal, State, local regulations, and tort law affecting the agencys Risk Management programs.

  • Proficiency on PC and knowledgeable of risk management, data analysis, and basic office software applications, and/or the ability to quickly learn and become proficient in new software systems specific to DART and risk management.
  • Analytical and creative skills to find solutions to complex interpersonal, technical, and administrative problems.
  • Ability to be dedicated to meeting the expectations and requirements of internal and external customers; acts with customers in mind; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect.

Anticipates and adjusts for problems and roadblocks. Measures performance against goals. Evaluates results.

Professionals:

07 - Skilled Craft (EEO-4-United States of America), 7A - Skilled Craft Workers (EEO-SubCategory)

General Summary:

Responsible for overseeing the programs and activities of Signal Systems personnel engaged in Signal Systems maintenance and for the complex Signal System testing, preventive maintenance, inspection, troubleshooting, upgrades and repair of train signaling systems, track switch machines, and grade crossing apparatus for Dallas Area Rapid Transit (DART) Ways, Structures and Amenities of the Maintenance Division.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversees personnel maintaining DARTs Signal Systems; assists in developing and training Signal Maintainers.

  • Evaluate Signal inspections and preventative maintenance and makes work assignments accordingly.

  • Troubleshoot and repair/replace the fiber optics network used for the Signal System.

  • Troubleshoot and repair/replace microprocessors, computers, recorder/analyzing equipment, and interpret and analyze data.

  • Maintained, troubleshoot, and repaired/replaced electrical equipment using voltages ranging from 12vdc to 480 vacs.

  • Knowledge to perform necessary programming of microprocessor-based Signal System components and complex tests on Signal Systems.

  • Monitor material usage, preventative and corrective maintenance databases, and the work order system.

  • Maintains and monitors spare parts inventory, equipment, tools, test equipment, and safety equipment.

  • Knowledge of interpreting circuit configurations and integrated circuit flow diagrams to develop and implement effective solutions for operational faults of Signal subsystems and components.

  • Perform signal tests and evaluations as required to certify compliance with reliability, maintainability, and safety criteria per DART standards.

  • Install, repair, maintain, and remove/replace components of the signal system, which include all associated signal equipment, such as highway grade crossing equipment, interlocking devices, cab signaling equipment (ATP), train to the wayside (TWC), vital/non-vital processors, fiber optic network, power distribution centers, UPS (uninterruptible power supplies), and other signal apparatus related to rail service.

  • Responsible for safely functioning signal equipment governing train movement during repairs, renewals, or replacement and promptly responding to all signal-related occurrences and/or emergency situations.

  • Oversees system performance and provides solutions to problems.

  • Promotes and enforces established training, safety practices, and procedures and takes necessary precautions.

  • Comply with AREMA, FRA, APTA, FTA rules and regulations, and DART safety requirements, rules, and regulations.

  • Interfaces with city technicians, vendors, and internal and external contacts. Maintain proper communication with Rail Operation Control while on duty.

  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE SKILLS AND ABILITIES REQUIRED:

Note: An equivalent combination of related education and experience may be substituted for the below-stated minimums excluding High School Diploma, GED, Licenses, or Certifications.

  • Associate's Degree from an accredited college, university, or technical institute in Business Administration, Computer Science, Rail Technology, Rail Signal Systems Civil/Electrical/Mechanical engineering, or other related technical fields.

  • Three (3) years experience in preventative and corrective Signal maintenance on an electrified rail transit system or Class I Railroad. Must pass a technical test.

  • Must obtain and maintain certification in compliance with all state and federal regulations applicable to this position.

  • Must have a valid Driver's License Class-C and be able to obtain a Texas Commercial Drivers License (CDL) Class-A Restricted within 90 days of employment; no Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) conviction within the last sixty (60) consecutive months, not more than one (1) DWI/DUI on driving record, and not more than three (3) convictions of moving violations within the last thirty-six (36) consecutive months to operate DART non-revenue vehicles. Operates DART non-revenue vehicles as required, such as crane and bucket trucks, flatbeds, trailers, etc.

  • Applicants/employees must pass and maintain a Department of Transportation (DOT) physical (medical) examination including pre-employment drug test and must submit to Federal Transportation Administration-required random drug/alcohol testing as a condition of continued employment.

  • Proficient in personal computer (PC), software applications to include MS Office (Word, Excel, Access).

  • Must be able to communicate effectively with the public, co-workers, supervisors, and managers to ensure efficient operations, promote safety, and respond to emergencies. Must also be able to read and comprehend a variety of work-related/required technical manuals, safety rules, and regulations.

  • Ability to have the functional and technical knowledge and skills to do the job at a high level of accomplishment.

  • Ability to make decisions in the absence of guidance from others and to plan and carry out work assignments in situations where the procedures have been established.

  • Must have excellent customer service skills and interact effectively with a diverse customer population under pressure.

  • Ability to be tolerant of people and processes. Listens and checks before acting.

  • Ability to work variable shifts, irregular hours, nights, holidays, weekends, and short notice availability. May be required to travel to multiple work locations. Physical ability to be mobile 100% of work time, exert physical effort while standing, walking, or lifting materials/tools/objects weighing up to 100. The position requires working in crowded and tight spaces, tunnels, and aerial structures.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Works in an environment where there is potential exposure to dust, noise, or temperature. Work could involve unpleasant working conditions such as working near fast-moving trains and in confined spaces, dust, noise, temperature, weather, petroleum products, and chemicals while visiting DART's operating facilities. All incumbent exposures will be controlled by adhering to policies and procedures, including safety precautions, regulations, and personal protective equipment.

Note: The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. The statements are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. All employees may perform other duties as assigned.

DART is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, supporting diversity in the workplace. M/F/D/V
